chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a woman who had a husband absent from her, then married another husband, so he said:

If she is brought before the Imam, then witnesses testify against her that she has an absent husband, and that his maintenance and news reach her from him, and that she has married another husband, then it is upon the Imam to administer the legal punishment to her and separate her from the one who married her.

I said: What about the dower that she took from him—what is to be done with it? He said: If he obtained something from her, then she may take it; but if he did not obtain anything from her, then everything she took from him is forbidden to her, like the wage of a fornicatress.

key_terms.أَجْرِ الْفَاجِرَةِ: the wage of a fornicatress, used here to describe unlawful gain
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the lawful authority before whom the case is brought and who implements the ruling
key_terms.الْمَهْرُ: the dower given in the marriage contract
key_terms.حَرَامٌ: forbidden or unlawful for her to keep
key_terms.شُهُودٌ: witnesses who testify to establish the facts of the case
key_terms.مَادَّتَهُ: his maintenance or provision reaching her from the absent husband
key_terms.يَحُدَّهَا: to administer the prescribed legal punishment to her
key_terms.يُفَرِّقَ: to separate the woman from the second man she married

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman marries another man while her absent husband is still alive and supporting her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a woman whose absent husband is still known to be living and providing support, yet she marries another man. It states that if the matter is established before the Imam through witnesses, the prescribed legal consequences are to be carried out, the two are to be separated, and the ruling on the mahr depends on whether consummation occurred.
